name: Gazetteer Named Place Ingest Nodes
description: The ORCHESTRATION half of the GeoNames gazetteer lane (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only between modules, no JSON and no base64): the schedule, the same-data ledger, the storage attribution and the resume mark, mirroring the cell-tower-source / cell-tower-ingest split. A daily TimerTick (TICK) enters mark_query, which emits the $FSO reading the newest $IRM resume marks through hostcap/flatsql-query (SELECT _data FROM IRM ORDER BY _rowid DESC LIMIT ? over the code-named view; the JSON lane's geonames_ingest_mark table exists on no node); ingest_plan reads the $FSB result, picks this dataset's mark by JOB_ID (geonames-ingest/<dataset id>) and plans the tick: the SEED (no mark: the ranged cities15000.zip plus admin1CodesASCII.txt, admin2Codes.txt and countryInfo.txt), the DELTA (seeded: modifications-<day>.txt with the mark's ETag as if-none-match, and deletes-<day>.txt) or NOTHING (the day is already on the mark). Each fetch is an HttpRequest (HREQ) whose CONTEXT carries the job, one size-prefixed $GNP header record (the dataset contract every record is published under), echoed by hostcap/http-request and read by geonames-source. ingest_meta authors the hostcap/storage-ingest IngestRequest (INGQ: SCHEMA GNP.fbs, PROVIDER_ID / SOURCE_NAME / BATCH_ID <dataset>@<day> / SOURCE_URL, RECONCILE None, PROVENANCE with the response's status, ETag, Last-Modified, RETRIEVED_MS and the record count) and forwards the $GNP stream untouched, refusing a seed whose Content-Range total exceeds the host's 4 MiB body cap; publish_request advances the mark FROM THE STORAGE RESULT (an $IRM: STATE COMPLETE, SOURCE = the edition with its ETag / Last-Modified, SOURCE_VERSION = the DATASET_EPOCH), never on a refused or stored-nothing batch, and - only when geonames_publish_url is set - POSTs the dataset-publication request whose body is the IngestResult naming the batch. Node CONFIG through plugin.getConfig (SDS $PIV ConfigEntry list): geonames_base_url, geonames_dataset_id, geonames_dataset_name, geonames_seed_dataset, geonames_seed_max_bytes (clamped to 4 MiB), geonames_http_timeout_ms, geonames_license, geonames_license_url, geonames_attribution, geonames_share_alike, geonames_non_commercial_only, geonames_id_prefix, geonames_provider_id, geonames_source_name, geonames_publish_url, geonames_mark_sql, geonames_mark_scan_rows. No credentials: capabilities none.

sequentialJustification.detail: Each method turns its typed frames into typed frames in one pass: one $FSO per tick, at most four requests per tick, one IngestRequest per batch, one mark (and at most one POST) per stored batch. No state is kept between invocations (the loop's state is the durable $IRM mark), no worker pool and no thread.

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (module-sdk runtime type TICK) from the flow's daily timer trigger.

$FSO (SDS FSO) for hostcap/flatsql-query query: OPERATION QUERY_RECORDS, QUERY = geonames_mark_sql (default SELECT _data FROM IRM ORDER BY _rowid DESC LIMIT ?), PARAMETERS = one FlatSQL tagged int64 (tag 2) = geonames_mark_scan_rows (default 32), PARAMETER_COUNT 1.

outputPorts.description: The FlatSQL read of the newest $IRM resume marks; ingest_plan picks this dataset's by JOB_ID.

methods.description: Builds the FlatSQL query that reads the resume marks back. A SEPARATE node from ingest_plan on purpose: the plan takes the mark as an INPUT, and a node that emitted its own input would be a cycle in the flow graph. The newest few $IRM records are read so one shared relation can hold every lane's marks. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE (except a flatsql-query result, whose $FSB chunks are all read). maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

acceptedTypeSets.description: $FSB (SDS FSB) chunks from hostcap/flatsql-query query records: KIND QUERY_RESULT, DATA = the aligned size-prefixed result stream (reassembled by CHUNK_SEQUENCE from 0); the $IRM records in it whose JOB_ID is geonames-ingest/<dataset id> are this lane's marks, the highest SEQUENCE winning.

inputPorts.description: The resume marks read back by flatsql-query, carrying the last stored edition and the upstream ETag. Absent (or no record of this dataset) on the first run.

methods.description: Decides between three outcomes and only three. FIRST TICK (no mark of this dataset, or one that never completed) = the SEED: one ranged fetch of the seed archive plus three for the division and country files, because $GNP carries a RESOLVED admin and country NAME beside every code. EVERY LATER TICK = the DELTA for the tick's own UTC day: modifications-YYYY-MM-DD.txt (full 19-column geoname rows, verified live 2026-08-15) and deletes-YYYY-MM-DD.txt. A TICK FOR A DAY ALREADY ON THE MARK emits nothing at all - the cheapest possible no-op. The date comes from the TICK, never a guest clock, and a tick that cannot be dated is refused (missing-tick-date): $GNP.SOURCE.DATASET_EPOCH is required on every record. A mark of another dataset is another JOB_ID and is never resumed from. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE (except a flatsql-query result, whose $FSB chunks are all read). maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (module-sdk runtime type INGQ) for hostcap/storage-ingest: SCHEMA GNP.fbs; TAGS PROVIDER_ID geonames_provider_id, SOURCE_NAME geonames_source_name, BATCH_ID <dataset id>@<YYYY-MM-DD>, SOURCE_URL; RECONCILE None (stored as given: a daily upsert must never retire the rest of the gazetteer); PROVENANCE SOURCE_URL, HTTP_STATUS, ETAG, LAST_MODIFIED, CONTENT_TYPE, RETRIEVED_MS, PARSER geonames-ingest-wasm v1, NORMALIZED_COUNT = records, SCHEMAS [GNP.fbs] / SCHEMA_COUNTS.

acceptedTypeSets.description: Size-prefixed $GNP FlatBuffer record stream, forwarded byte-for-byte (for storage-ingest gnp_records).

methods.description: Authors the attribution the storage lane cannot invent - dataset, source, ONE batch per edition (<dataset id>@<day>, so re-running a day is idempotent and two days never collide) - from the job the main fetch's response carries, and reads the three facts only the RESPONSE carries. A job without DATASET_ID, SOURCE_URL and DATASET_EPOCH is refused (incomplete-job-attribution). THE SEED MUST NOT BE SILENTLY TRUNCATED: when Content-Range's denominator proves the archive is larger than the range asked for (geonames_seed_max_bytes, clamped to the host's 4 MiB), the run is refused (seed-exceeds-host-body-cap) rather than inflating a prefix into a plausible short gazetteer. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE (except a flatsql-query result, whose $FSB chunks are all read). maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

acceptedTypeSets.description: $IRM (SDS IRM, Ingest Resume Mark): JOB_ID geonames-ingest/<dataset id>, SEQUENCE = the edition's day number since 1970-01-01, PROVIDER_ID, INGESTOR_ID com.digitalarsenal.data-source.geonames-ingest, SOURCE (SOURCE_URL, ENTITY_TAG = the ETag, LAST_MODIFIED, SOURCE_VERSION = the DATASET_EPOCH), STATE COMPLETE, LAST_CHUNK (BATCH_ID, RECORDS_DECODED, RECORDS_STORED, COMMITTED_AT), CHUNKS_COMMITTED 1, RECORDS_COMMITTED, TARGET_STANDARD $GNP, RECONCILE_MODE none, UPDATED_AT / COMPLETED_AT, TAGS date:<YYYY-MM-DD> and lane:<seed|delta>. A record for hostcap/storage-write write_record.

outputPorts.description: The advanced resume mark, carrying the stored edition and the upstream ETag that makes the next tick a ledgered no-op.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (HREQ) for hostcap/http-request: POST geonames_publish_url, content-type application/octet-stream, BODY = an IngestResult (INGR) FlatBuffer naming the batch (SCHEMA, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, BATCH_ID, INSERTED, ...).

outputPorts.description: Dataset-publication POST announcing this epoch; emitted ONLY when a publish URL is configured.

methods.description: Advances the resume mark FROM THE STORAGE RESULT - never at dispatch, so a crash between fetch and store re-fetches one day instead of skipping it invisibly. A REFUSED batch (ingest-refused) and THE SILENT NOP - inserted=0 for an edition that carried records (ingest-stored-nothing) - advance nothing and ledger no ETag; a genuinely empty edition (no records in) still advances. The mark is NOT gated on publication; the epoch announce is fail-closed without geonames_publish_url and mints no new record type: DATASET_EPOCH already rides in $GNP.SOURCE on every stored record. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE (except a flatsql-query result, whose $FSB chunks are all read). maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.
